work.text: A program that solves a coding problem. A validator posts a signed task to the miner's HTTP endpoint and the miner returns a Python or Rust solution before the deadline. The included demo miner forwards the task to a hosted GLM-5.2 model. What is paid for is a solution that passes every hidden test case, which the miner never sees.
work.quote: Validators lease a public coding challenge, rotation-deal it to half of the serving miners, commit the signed responses, reveal the hidden tests

scoring.text: All or nothing, then speed. The validator commits the exact signed answers to the problem server before it may see the hidden cases, then runs each answer in a one-CPU, 256 MiB Docker container with no network. The fastest fully correct answer is paid 1.0; every three minutes of extra latency halves the part above 0.95. Anything short of the full suite pays 0. Peer pass rates do not matter.

split.text: Proportional. A miner's score is the mean of its last 200 completed-problem payments, with a floor divisor of 4 so a couple of early wins cannot show as a full score. Validators normalize those means to sum to one and submit them as weights with no owner reservation; the policy refuses a non-zero owner burn share. A miner absent when sampled records a zero. History is keyed by hotkey.

judges.text: Nine validators were active on the 2026-09-09 chain snapshot. Commit-reveal is off. Each validator is a whole examiner: it leases problems from a private problem server outside the repository, deals each to half of the serving miners in rotation, commits the signed replies, receives the hidden cases and grades every reply itself in a sandbox. The server can pace validators with Retry-After and gates the reveal.
judges.quote: commit_reveal_weights_enabled False, weights_rate_limit 100, weights_version 803; chain-2026-09-09.json active_validators 9

cadence.text: Emission settles every 360 blocks, about 72 minutes. A validator attempts a challenge every 38 blocks, about 7.5 minutes, and submits weights every 180 blocks, about 36 minutes, never below the chain rate limit plus 20. A miner is judged on a rolling window of its last 200 problems. A new registration is immune from deregistration for 5,000 blocks, about 16 hours.
cadence.quote: tempo 360, immunity_period 5000; policy.py round_interval_blocks: int = 38, weights_interval_blocks: int = 180

buyer.text: Looked for a price, a customer, a product page or an endpoint on honedashboard.com, a miner-performance dashboard that renders Waiting for aggregate data to a fetcher, and in the README, DESIGN.md and DEMO_MINER.md at the pinned commit. None found. The README says problem construction is not part of this repository; the only hint of an output beyond weights is that partial-credit rewards affect exported dataset labels.

exploits.text: Leaking hidden tests into a prompt: the signed answer set is committed before the cases are revealed. Replaying a captured request: an 8-second UUID cache. Inheriting a good history: scores are keyed by hotkey and cleared on change. Copying another miner's solution: not addressed; the code says AST fingerprints were rejected because they reward irrelevant structural changes, so V1 has no duplication scoring. Timeouts and invalid replies score zero.
exploits.quote: TODO(V2): Revisit duplication-resistant scoring only with a signal that cannot be cheaply gamed.
